editions.title: Tesla and SpaceX explore merger; PHP emergency patches loom
editions.notification: Musk backs a Tesla-SpaceX merger, with special committees formed. Nothing agreed yet. Here's where it stands.
editions.intro:
The biggest story is Elon Musk's public backing for a possible merger between Tesla and SpaceX. He said on an earnings call that both companies have formed special committees to assess a deal, while stressing that nothing is agreed. Reported valuations of roughly $1.5tn for Tesla and $2tn for SpaceX would make it the largest merger on record. Any deal would need majority shareholder approval, and a Reuters exclusive suggests Musk's public push could complicate talks. Insiders reportedly fear it could invite shareholder scrutiny and delay talks by several weeks, drawing comparisons to the litigation-heavy 2016 SolarCity deal.

Security is the other major thread. Serious flaws in PHP, the language behind many websites including Wikipedia and WordPress, were found with AI tools. Patches are due imminently, and AWS says attackers tried to exploit the bugs days before disclosure. Governments and agencies including the US NSA and UK NCSC have urged immediate updates or taking systems offline, and several sites have already gone dark. Administrators should patch or isolate systems now.

Elsewhere, Meta says its Muse personal AI agent is entering a scaling phase, with more than 10 million users and plans for commerce fees and subscriptions. Tesla says it will start selling Cybercabs by year-end, though a US safety investigation could affect whether the vehicle can legally operate. Apple has been ordered to open iPhone app distribution in Australia from March 2027, and Apple says it will appeal. Apple also reportedly raised its iPhone Duo foldable production target by about 44%.

top_stories.title: Musk backs Tesla-SpaceX merger; special committees formed
top_stories.summary: Musk said he favours a merger of Tesla and SpaceX and that special committees are assessing a deal, with no guarantee and nothing agreed. Valuations of about $1.5tn and $2tn would make it the largest merger ever, and a majority of Tesla's shares would be needed for approval.

top_stories.title: Musk's endorsement may complicate merger talks
top_stories.summary: A source says the public push has troubled some insiders, who fear shareholder scrutiny could delay talks by several weeks. Advisers are hired and structures including an all-stock deal are under discussion.

top_stories.title: Global scramble after PHP flaws found using AI
top_stories.summary: Serious PHP flaws, found by researchers using AI tools, prompted agencies including the NSA and NCSC to urge immediate updates or taking systems offline. Wikimedia and several governments and the BBC took sites down as a precaution.

top_stories.title: PHP maintainers say two emergency patches are imminent
top_stories.summary: Two flaws rated 9.2 out of 10 will be patched within about twelve hours after leaked exploit details surfaced. Researchers expect mass attacks soon after release, potentially affecting around 1.3 million hosts.

top_stories.title: Zuckerberg says Meta's Muse enters a scaling phase
top_stories.summary: Meta's personal AI agent has over 10 million users since its early September US and Canada rollout. Commerce fees and AI subscriptions are planned, and Zuckerberg predicts Muse could eventually out-earn Facebook and Instagram per user.

top_stories.title: Tesla to start selling Cybercabs by year-end
top_stories.summary: Tesla plans to begin customer sales of the Cybercab later this year, initially small. A NHTSA investigation into whether the vehicle meets manual-control safety standards could determine whether it can legally operate.

top_stories.title: Apple ordered to open iPhone apps in Australia
top_stories.summary: A federal court ordered Apple to allow alternative app stores and websites for Australian users from 1 March 2027. Apple says it will appeal and seek a stay, while Epic says Fortnite will return to the Australian App Store.

editions.title: Musk floats Tesla-SpaceX merger; CoreWeave slides on GPU price rise
editions.notification: Musk says Tesla and SpaceX merger is being assessed, with special committees formed. Nothing agreed yet.
editions.intro:
The biggest story is Elon Musk's confirmation that Tesla and SpaceX have each formed special committees to assess a possible merger. Musk stressed that nothing has been agreed. Tesla is valued at about $1.5tn and SpaceX at $2tn, which would make it the largest merger on record. Any deal would need Tesla shareholder approval from a majority of all outstanding shares, a hurdle Musk himself called high. Critics argue it would dilute shareholders, and regulators may take a close look.

AI infrastructure was under pressure. CoreWeave shares fell below $60, their lowest since May 2025, after a report said the company had raised hourly GPU prices by a further 10% on top of a July rise of about 25%. The firm owes roughly $50bn, and some bond yields have topped 15%. Rising inflation has raised the prospect of a Federal Reserve rate hike, which weighs on borrowing-heavy AI firms. Nvidia is reportedly in talks to invest hundreds of millions of dollars in Firmus Grid, an Australian AI cloud firm that pulled its IPO, a sign it still backs neoclouds.

Supermicro gave a strong preliminary update, with quarterly revenue of $18.5bn to $19.5bn against earlier guidance of $14.5bn to $15.5bn, though the figures are unaudited. Elsewhere, Microsoft's next Xbox plans, including a 2027 handheld, a 2028 console called Project Helix and a possible à la carte Game Pass, remain unconfirmed rumours.

top_stories.summary: Musk said both companies have formed special committees to look at a possible merger, which would be the largest ever at about $3.5tn combined. editions.title: Anthropic and Nscale in $45bn talks; Anthropic IPO chatter grows
editions.notification: Anthropic and Nscale reportedly in talks on a $45bn compute deal. Here's what we know.
editions.intro:
The biggest story in the last 24 hours is a reported $45 billion cloud computing deal under discussion between AI developer Anthropic and Nvidia-backed Nscale. Bloomberg, Reuters and others all report that talks are under way, but no terms, timing or confirmation have come from either company. If it goes ahead, it would be a major commitment of computing capacity and a notable signal for AI infrastructure spending, though talks could still change or fail.

Anthropic is also back in the headlines over its possible listing. Bloomberg reports that former Google chief executive Eric Schmidt holds roughly a 1% stake, bought in the 2021 Series A, and that IPO marketing could start as early as the week of 9 November. Neither Schmidt nor Anthropic has commented, and the claims remain unverified. Sea Ltd's reported move into enterprise cloud and a possible fintech listing also points to companies trying to find new growth.

Elsewhere, Google said four Gemini agents completed Minecraft without human help, and Arm made performance claims against AMD's server chips that rest on modelled projections. A tipped Apple autumn event and a record $5.7 billion patent verdict against Apple add to the news flow. A South Korean data centre builder's 33% stock fall on debut is a reminder that investors are growing wary of stretched AI valuations.

top_stories.summary: Bloomberg reports talks between Nscale and Anthropic on a cloud computing deal worth about $45 billion. Reuters and others carry similar reports, but no terms, timing or confirmation have been published. A deal of this size would be a major compute commitment to a leading AI developer, though talks may still fail.

top_stories.summary: Bloomberg reports Schmidt's stake dates from a 2021 Series A investment, with a private fair value of $1.8 to $2 trillion cited. Anthropic reportedly plans IPO marketing as early as November, but neither party has commented and the figures are unverified.

top_stories.summary: Japan's H3 rocket launched the MMX spacecraft, which will study Mars' moons and attempt Phobos landings in 2029. A sample return capsule is due in South Australia in 2031, which officials describe as the first sample return from the Martian moons.

top_stories.summary: Taction has asked a judge for extra damages on iPhone and Apple Watch sales from 2026, plus interest. Apple denies wrongdoing and is challenging the jury verdict, which could carry significant financial consequences if it stands.

top_stories.summary: Arm says its data centre CPU delivers roughly twice the per-rack performance of AMD's EPYC 9755 in agentic AI tests. The rack figure is a modelled projection, and the results apply only to the selected configurations, verified by Signal65 in an Arm-commissioned analysis.

editions.title: Nscale loses Microsoft anchor as AI stocks wobble
editions.notification: Microsoft reportedly quits Nscale's Essex data centre as AI infrastructure stocks slide. Here's what it means.
editions.intro:
The biggest story of the period is a setback for Nscale, the British AI infrastructure firm preparing a New York listing. The Telegraph reports that Microsoft has pulled out as anchor tenant of its Loughton data centre in Essex, reportedly because grid officials said power would not arrive until the 2030s. Nscale says it remains committed to the site and is exploring alternative power. The timing is awkward: Microsoft and Anthropic account for about 85% of its contracts, and the reported $35bn valuation now faces scrutiny. The report also lands in a broader cooling of AI infrastructure sentiment, with a separate report finding at least 47 AI infrastructure projects hit setbacks this year.

Markets are feeling the same nerves. Japanese stocks fell at the open as a chip-led tech selloff deepened on doubts about the AI trade, and a Korean pension fund reportedly lost about $137bn after Samsung and SK Hynix slid. Commentators expect Magnificent Seven earnings to test whether hyperscaler AI spending holds up. Chinese data showed growth of 4.5% in the third quarter, with AI-related exports offsetting weak domestic demand and a property slump, which gives Beijing room for support measures.

Elsewhere, Apple dominated the rumour mill: reports point to touchscreen MacBooks and an OLED iPad mini arriving around 6 November, and a robotic 360-degree HomeView display, though none of this is confirmed. Its new foldable iPhone Duo is in heavy demand, with walk-in stock reportedly unlikely on launch day. Google unveiled a Gemini 4 agent team that completed Minecraft autonomously, while Meta said a Claude-linked tool wrongly suspended a protest group's Instagram account.

top_stories.summary: The Telegraph reports Microsoft has dropped its anchor role at Nscale's Loughton site, citing grid delays into the 2030s. Nscale says it remains committed and is seeking alternative power. The news lands just after its New York IPO filing, with Microsoft and Anthropic making up about 85% of contracts.

top_stories.title: Tech selloff deepens in Japan on AI doubts
top_stories.summary: Japanese stocks fell at the open as chip names led declines, with investors questioning the viability of the AI trade. The feed gave no index levels, but the move follows a weak week for AI infrastructure names. Magnificent Seven earnings are seen as the next test.

top_stories.title: Korean pension fund hit by $137bn loss
top_stories.summary: Bloomberg reports South Korea's main pension fund lost 182 trillion won as Samsung and SK Hynix shares fell. The scale shows how dependent the fund is on its largest chipmakers. It underlines the market risk from the current chip slide.

top_stories.title: China's Q3 growth edges up to 4.5% on AI exports
top_stories.summary: China grew 4.5% in the third quarter, the bottom of its target range, with AI-related chip exports offsetting weak domestic spending. Property investment fell more than 20% in the first nine months. Beijing has announced support measures, giving policymakers room to act.

top_stories.summary: POLITICO reports Anthropic has privately offered lawmakers a draft frontier AI bill allowing federal halts only for imminent, severe risks. It would give Commerce sole halt power and override some state laws. The move fuels debate over AI firms writing their own rules.

top_stories.title: UK watchdog proposes strategic status for Microsoft
top_stories.summary: The CMA proposes designating Microsoft with Strategic Market Status in business software, citing switching difficulty for around 20 million UK users. Possible remedies include changes to bundling, licensing and interoperability. Microsoft says its products are open and it will keep engaging.

editions.title: Nscale loses Microsoft anchor as AI infrastructure jitters deepen
editions.notification: Microsoft reportedly walks away from Nscale's Essex data centre weeks before its New York IPO.
editions.intro:
The biggest story is a setback for Nscale, the British AI infrastructure firm. The Telegraph reports that Microsoft has pulled out as anchor tenant of its Loughton data centre in Essex, where grid power is reportedly not due until the 2030s. The news lands just after Nscale filed for a New York IPO under the ticker NSCL, with a float that could value it at up to $35bn. Microsoft and Anthropic make up about 85% of its contracts, so investors will watch delivery schedules closely. Nscale says it remains committed to Loughton and that its Microsoft relationship is strong. Microsoft has not commented.

The wider backdrop is a broad selloff in AI-linked shares. Japanese stocks fell as chip names led declines, Korean markets were hit hard, and South Korea's main pension fund reportedly lost about $137bn. Concern about whether AI spending will pay off also weighed on Oracle, Nvidia and neocloud peers. Analysts say Magnificent Seven earnings may test whether hyperscaler spending confidence holds. Meanwhile, the OpenAI Stargate project reportedly faces major obstacles, and Elon Musk again mocked the plan.

There are some firmer signals. Nvidia shares were set to end a three-day losing streak on a report that ByteDance and Tencent have each received H200 chips, and reports say Samsung and SK hynix may unveil a very large multi-year investment plan. Apple's iPhone Duo is dominating headlines, with supply strain, delayed shipping dates and a battery figure now confirmed, while Apple's AI features are reportedly set for China in December.

editions.title: Microsoft quits Nscale site as AI trade wobbles and iPhone Duo supply strains
editions.intro:
The biggest story is a reported setback for Nscale, the British AI cloud startup. The Telegraph reports that Microsoft has pulled out of a deal to anchor Nscale's first UK data centre in Loughton, Essex, weeks before Nscale's planned IPO of up to $3bn. Nscale says it remains committed to the site and that its Microsoft relationship is strong, and Microsoft has not commented. The report lands as investors grow wary of neocloud firms, and CoreWeave shares were marked down in coverage of the story.

The wider backdrop is a deepening selloff in US tech shares. Bloomberg reports that this is exposing weak spots in Asia's AI "picks and shovels" suppliers, with rising financing costs threatening data-centre and hardware spending. The FT also argues that America's roughly $10tn AI infrastructure build-out is running into physical constraints. Against that, SemiAnalysis says more than 300 local data-centre moratoriums have delayed only a few projects so far. Meta's earnings, previewed by the FT as a test of confidence in AI spending, are the next major read-across.

Apple dominated the rest of the day's flow. The iPhone Duo, its first foldable, is reportedly sold out into January, with staff told walk-in buyers are unlikely to get stock on launch day, and Gurman calls the staggered pre-order rollout a "major mistake". Apple's EU energy label put the device's battery at 4,883 mAh. Rumours also point to a touchscreen MacBook and a HomeView smart display with a robotic arm, with a possible retail refresh on 6 November. Most of these remain unconfirmed.

top_stories.title: Microsoft reportedly quits Nscale UK data centre before IPO
top_stories.summary: The Telegraph reports Microsoft has pulled out of anchoring Nscale's first British site in Loughton, weeks before a planned IPO of up to $3bn. Nscale says it remains committed and Microsoft has not commented. The story reflects investor caution around neocloud firms.

top_stories.title: AI trade reversal hits Asia's picks-and-shovels stocks
top_stories.summary: Bloomberg reports a deepening US tech selloff is exposing weak spots in Asia's AI supply chain. Rising financing costs could curb data-centre and hardware spending, putting regional supplier earnings at risk.

top_stories.title: America's $10tn AI infrastructure boom meets physical limits
top_stories.summary: The FT argues the AI build-out is running into the hard economics of power, equipment and data-centre construction. It is a broad analysis rather than a single announcement, but it frames the spending debate ahead of Meta's results.

top_stories.title: Meta earnings seen as test of AI investment confidence
top_stories.summary: The FT's weekly preview asks whether Meta's results can restore confidence in the AI spending boom. Investors will watch closely given the scale of Meta's AI outlays.

top_stories.title: iPhone Duo walk-in buying likely hard at launch
top_stories.summary: Apple Store staff reportedly told customers without pre-orders to expect no launch-day stock. Apple says demand is extraordinary, and shipping estimates have slipped to around late January in most countries.

top_stories.title: Nvidia reportedly standardises custom HBM base die on TSMC 3nm
top_stories.summary: A single unnamed report says Nvidia asked Samsung, Micron and SK hynix to build custom HBM base dies on TSMC's 3nm node, with Samsung reportedly accepting. The claimed gains are unverified but would mark a shift in memory supply.

top_stories.title: Samsung may switch Galaxy S27 Ultra away from Snapdragon
top_stories.summary: Seoul Economic Daily reports Samsung told Qualcomm its Snapdragon chip misses performance targets due to overheating, and that its own 2nm Exynos 2700 did better. Qualcomm denies the report, which rests on unnamed sources.

rumour_watch.note: Single unnamed source and unverified figures, but Samsung's reported acceptance of a shared base-die approach would be a notable supply-chain shift if confirmed.
Credible-sounding but thinly sourced and directly denied by Qualcomm, so treat the Exynos switch as speculative.
Bloomberg's Mark Gurman has a strong record on Apple hardware, but the 2027-28 timing and product names are explicitly speculative.
Multiple sources, including Gurman, point to a touchscreen MacBook around early November, but Apple has not confirmed any date.

in_brief.line: Reports say the FTC has issued demands to OpenAI and Anthropic; the demands are not a finding of wrongdoing.
Character.AI has filed for bankruptcy, with Disney agreeing to offer jobs to at least 60 staff in a stalking-horse bid.

FT reports Accenture is exploring a sale of its China operations for up to $1.5bn; no buyer or terms yet.

Anthropic backs a federal AI safety bill that would only allow blocking releases for risks above $1bn damage or 50+ casualties.
Anthropic's internal study shows junior hiring fell sharply as its AI agents logged six times the human work hours.

Finance.title: Tech rebound, SpaceX results and Iran-linked oil pressure
Finance.notification: SpaceX's first quarterly profit lifts Asian tech, but oil and Middle East risk keep investors wary.
Finance.summary:
The dominant theme is a volatile tech trade. SpaceX reported its first quarterly profit as a listed company, with net profit of $4.4 billion and revenue up 161% to $14.6 billion. That helped lift chipmakers and AI-related firms in Asia, with SK hynix and Samsung rising at least 7%, and Super Micro jumped after preliminary results beat forecasts. Elon Musk also backed a possible SpaceX-Tesla merger, though this remains a rumour with no confirmed terms.

The rally was patchy. Earlier in the week, concerns over AI spending and the cost of it had hit Asian tech, and Meta and Tesla earnings revived those worries. Oil is the other pressure point: Brent has traded around $108 to $111, with reports of a tanker struck off Qatar, the Financial Times reporting that Netanyahu is pushing to resume strikes on Iran, and BofA warning of a possible supply crunch within months. Hong Kong stocks are heading for a four-month low as stimulus hopes fade.

Energy policy is also in focus in the UK. The government approved the Jackdaw gas field, while the fate of the larger Rosebank oil field remains open, with reports that the Energy Secretary is leaning towards rejection. Meanwhile, UK inflation is expected to rise on fuel costs, which has raised the prospect of rate rises and weighed on mortgages.

points.text: UK CPI rose to 3.5% in September, and markets now price two rate rises before year end.
A New Mexico court ordered Meta to pay $25 billion over Facebook privacy violations.
Jackdaw approved; Rosebank decision pending, with reports the government leans towards rejecting it.
Netflix revenue rose 12%, but viewing has stagnated in the US and Canada, a concern for the company.
LSEG agreed to buy credit intelligence firm Octus from Permira for $3.5 billion in cash.
Sainsbury's raised its profit target floor but warned of tough conditions and slowing like-for-like sales.

World.title: Gulf escalation and Ukraine talks dominate world news
World.notification: US orders diplomats out of Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks escalate and oil climbs
World.summary:
The most consequential story is the escalating conflict around Saudi Arabia. The US has ordered non-emergency staff and their families to leave the kingdom after Houthi strikes killed three people, including one at Dammam airport, and the UK is sending Typhoon jets to help defend it. The Houthis have targeted airports, energy sites and military bases since an informal ceasefire collapsed in July. The fighting is tied to the wider Iran war and Red Sea disruption, and Iran's Revolutionary Guard Navy says seven vessels were hit and has warned Washington of a wider response. Oil prices are sensitive to this, and a Qatar-reported progress in US-Iran talks is a counterweight, though Tehran says it does not trust Washington.

Ukraine is the second thread. Steve Witkoff met Putin in St Petersburg, Russia and Ukraine traded large strikes, and the Kremlin says it may resume trilateral talks after 10 November, with a possible Trump-Putin-Xi meeting around APEC in Shenzhen. Analysts are sceptical of an imminent deal. US support for Kyiv has fallen sharply, with reports of a Starlink slowdown and a diesel deal with Moscow, though intelligence sharing has reportedly resumed. Europe is also absorbing unrest: France has seen its worst street violence in years, and Italy and Paris have imposed restrictions, while French 10-year yields near 5% reflect wider debt strain.

Taken together, the Gulf and Russia stories point to energy supply risk and sanctions uncertainty, while the European unrest and rising borrowing costs add to a cautious market backdrop. Gold has fallen as oil rallied and rate expectations firmed.

points.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Navy says seven vessels were hit and warns the US of a wider response.
Qatar reports progress in US-Iran talks, but Tehran says it does not trust Washington.
Italy approves 500 troops for Milan and tougher penalties after cost-of-living protests turned violent.
France rejects Trump's claim that migration caused the unrest, with over 2,000 detained.
France's 10-year yield near 5% is the highest since 2002, while global debt tops $365 trillion.
Zelenskyy says US intelligence sharing on Russian missile strikes has resumed.

Tech.title: Musk pushes Tesla–SpaceX merger as PHP flaws spread
Tech.notification: Musk backs a Tesla–SpaceX merger that could be the largest ever, while PHP flaws force websites offline.
Tech.summary:
The dominant story is Elon Musk's public backing of a possible merger between Tesla and SpaceX. He said both companies have formed special committees to assess a deal, while stressing that nothing is agreed and there is no guarantee. Tesla is valued at about $1.5tn and SpaceX at about $2tn, which would make it the largest merger on record. Any deal would need Tesla shareholder approval from a majority of shares. Analysts say it would combine Tesla's cars, robots and self-driving technology with SpaceX's rockets, satellites and data centres, but regulators and shareholders may scrutinise it. Insider concerns reported by Reuters suggest the public endorsement could complicate talks, and one critical commentary warns of dilution for shareholders.

A second major story is a serious security flaw in PHP, the language behind many websites. Researchers used AI tools to uncover the bugs, and government agencies including the US NSA and UK NCSC urged immediate patching or taking systems offline. Wikimedia, several councils and the BBC took sites down as a precaution. Reports say the flaws were already being probed before the planned disclosure, so exploitation is expected to continue.

Elsewhere, the AI infrastructure sector shows strain. CoreWeave shares fell below $60 after a reported further GPU price rise, and Nvidia is reportedly in talks to invest in the Australian AI cloud firm Firmus after its IPO was abandoned. Supermicro, by contrast, flagged quarterly revenue well above guidance.

points.text: Explainer: PHP flaws found with AI tools prompted a global alert, with patches released on Wednesday.
AWS says attempts to exploit the PHP bugs began four days before the public fixes.
CoreWeave dipped below $60, its lowest since May 2025, after a reported 10% GPU price rise.
Supermicro expects quarterly revenue of $18.5bn to $19.5bn, well above its earlier guidance.
Tesla says it will begin selling the Cybercab by year-end, though a NHTSA probe is open.
Reports say Microsoft's Project Helix console could cost $1,200 to $1,800 in 2028, unconfirmed.

Fashion.title: Luxury wobbles: China, Europe unrest and weak French trade
Fashion.notification: Protests hit Paris luxury stores as LVMH, Kering and Moncler feel the squeeze. Here is what it means for the sector.
Fashion.summary:
The clearest story for luxury is the strain on demand. Hundreds of stores in Paris and other French cities were looted during cost-of-living protests on 17 and 18 October, with luxury names including Saint Laurent, Celine, Dior and Louis Vuitton among those hit. Stores in Milan have closed and further protests are planned across Europe, so retailers are adding closures and security. Analysts are also pointing to weaker Chinese demand: LVMH reported a 5% fall in third-quarter fashion and leather goods sales, and Euromonitor says China's luxury fashion market is still well below its 2023 peak.

Other results fit the same pattern. Moncler's flat third-quarter revenue was blamed on weak tourist spending in Europe, while Ferragamo's revenue fell 3.5% in the quarter, with wholesale down sharply and a plan to close stores in lower-tier Chinese cities. SMCP's nine-month sales were broadly flat, with a steep fall in France offsetting growth in America and EMEA. Barclays' profits, though outside fashion, were also reported as held back.

Brands are still pushing ahead with launches and partnerships. Dior is opening a Harrods pop-up featuring Jonathan Anderson's first cruise collection, Adidas opened a premium store in Rome, and Gap is to receive a CFDA Innovation Award. The CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund went to Zane Li of Lii, who was also a Karl Lagerfeld Prize winner earlier this year.

points.text: Ferragamo's third-quarter revenue fell 3.5% to €207m, with wholesale down 19.1% over nine months and China still slowing.
SMCP's nine-month sales were flat at €888m, as a 10.4% organic fall in France offset growth in America and EMEA.
Moncler's flat third-quarter revenue was attributed to weak tourist spending in Europe, with no further figures available.
Vogue says Western luxury brands must justify premium pricing as China's market fragments and consumer confidence weakens.
Dior's Harrods pop-up runs from 6 November to 27 December, showing Jonathan Anderson's first cruise collection.
Zane Li of Lii won the 2026 CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund, with a $300,000 prize and mentorship.
